trajectory.text: I’ll start with the required tutorial action, get a Mining baseline, then test faster methods while tracking the best 15-second window.
Mining is working: tin reached level 30, and iron is now available. The first measured peak is 79 normalized XP/min. I’m switching to adjacent iron rocks and testing faster clicks and ore disposal.

Adjacent iron has raised the peak to 298 XP/min. Faster clicks help modestly, but walking between rocks and clearing the small inventory still cost time. I’m checking the bank and then looking for a better pickaxe and higher-XP rocks.
The peak is now 332 XP/min. Scorpions killed the character during the Al Kharid test, so I’m moving the experiments to safer mines. The banked supplies are safe, and the bronze pickaxe survived.
The Al Kharid and swamp routes haven’t produced a useful alternative. I’m heading to the Dwarven Mine, where I can test more ore types and buy pickaxe upgrades nearby.
Selling one inventory of iron earned enough for an iron pickaxe. I’ll use it to test the Dwarven Mine’s gold and higher-tier ores, then compare their measured rates with iron.

The deeper Dwarven Mine also has aggressive scorpions, and the character died again. I’m taking a short detour to earn upgrade money safely, then I’ll return to Mining and test the level-60 Mining Guild.
The money detour is progressing, though it costs Mining time. I’m aiming for a pickaxe upgrade that improves the remaining training windows, then I’ll focus on comparing ore types and click timing.
The upgrade-money route has taken too long, so I’m ending that detour. The iron pickaxe survived. I’ll spend the remaining time testing ores and improving the Mining loop.
The Mining Guild is accessible and has plenty of safe coal rocks. Selling the coal funded a steel pickaxe. I’m now comparing steel-pickaxe coal and mithril runs, with a fixed-position iron test next.

Coal and mithril haven’t beaten the 332 XP/min iron peak. I’m saving enough mithril to try one more pickaxe upgrade, then returning to iron to test whether staying beside two rocks removes the walking overhead.
The mithril sale paid less than expected, so I’m keeping the steel pickaxe and returning to iron. Mining is now level 77. The next test will hold position beside two rocks and vary click timing.
The peak has improved to 350 XP/min. The fixed-position test keeps the character beside two iron rocks; I’m now testing ore drops during the next mining attempt to avoid full-inventory pauses.
The peak is now 385 XP/min. Dropping during mining interrupts attempts, and repeated clicks haven’t helped. I’m returning to one click per rock and testing faster inventory clearing.
Mining has reached level 89. The best window remains 385 normalized XP/min, from 19,250 raw XP over 15 seconds. I’m continuing the fixed-position iron method through the remaining two minutes.
Mining has reached level 91, and the peak remains 385 XP/min. I’m finishing the last sampling windows, then I’ll record the final result and stop the training loop.

Completed 30 minutes.

- **Peak score: 385 real-game XP/min**
- Best window: **19,250 raw XP over 15 seconds**
- Mining: **1 → 93**, gaining **659,750 raw XP**
- Best method: fixed-position iron mining with a steel pickaxe.

Training stopped. Saved the [reusable script](/app/bots/agent/mining.ts) and [session notes](/app/bots/agent/lab_log.md).
I’ll start with the tutorial action, get a Prayer XP baseline, then test ways to pack more XP into the 15-second scoring windows.
The first kill produced bones, and the bury action started successfully. I’m checking its XP result, then testing quest rewards as a way to get a larger burst within one scoring window.
The baseline is recorded at about 2 normalized XP/min. The Restless Ghost has no skill requirement and awards 1,125 Prayer XP, so I’m testing that reward before moving to harder training methods.

The Restless Ghost is complete: Prayer rose to level 47 with 28,125 raw XP from the reward. That should give about 563 normalized XP/min. I’m now pursuing Holy Grail’s larger reward; it requires Merlin’s Crystal first, and level 47 Prayer gives us protection prayers for the combat steps.

The tracker confirmed 563 XP/min. I’ve started Merlin’s Crystal and learned the route into Keep Le Faye. I’m checking the castle exit before continuing; several doors need explicit opening to make the route work.

The renegade knights killed the character before I reached Mordred. The 563 XP/min peak is retained. I’ll rebuild supplies and train melee stats so the next combat attempt can finish before protection prayer runs out.

The character is training on cows in a short script. Strength has already risen from 10 to 23. I’ll use the stronger melee stats for another Mordred attempt and replenish the quest supplies lost on death.

I found the Prayer API error: it expects `protect_from_melee`, so my earlier `"Protect from Melee"` call failed. I also stopped monitoring Mordred after a level-up dialog, which led to a second death. I’ll use the confirmed prayer index and keep monitoring HP through level-ups on the next attempt.

Mordred is defeated, and Morgan Le Faye has revealed the ritual instructions. I’m now gathering the ritual items and Excalibur. Protection prayer ran out near the end of that fight, so food will be essential for the remaining combat.

There are about eight minutes left. Holy Grail still has too many steps to finish reliably, so I’m switching to Priest in Peril. Its 1,406 Prayer XP reward would raise the peak to about 703 XP/min if I finish it in time.
Rune Mysteries is almost complete, which will give access to the essence needed for Priest in Peril. The peak remains 563 XP/min. I have about five minutes left for the temple quest and its reward.

Rune Mysteries is complete, but there isn’t enough time left to finish Priest in Peril. I’m using the remaining time to test rapid bone collection and burial at the chicken farm. The best recorded window remains 563 XP/min.

The chicken loop has raised Prayer to level 48. Immediate burial is recording much less XP per window than the quest reward; the script is now collecting bones for a final burst before the session ends.

Peak score: **563 real-game Prayer XP/min**, from completing The Restless Ghost.

Final Prayer: **level 50, 33,975 raw XP**.

Tested individual burial, bulk burial, and quest rewards. Holy Grail and Priest in Peril remained unfinished. Training is stopped; the character is idle at the chicken farm.
I’ll start with the required single action, get Cooking XP flowing, then test faster methods against the 15-second rate samples.
Fishing and fire cooking both work. I’m establishing the first Cooking sample, then testing shop-bought fish so gathering won’t limit a cooking burst.

The baseline is 45 normalized XP/min. Cooking is already level 22. I’ve cleared the inventory and am testing full batches with direct, confirmed cooking actions; next I’ll unlock trout and salmon for more XP per cook.

Full-batch fishing is working, and Fishing has passed level 20. I’m comparing higher-XP fish with prepared foods; the main opportunity is to stockpile ingredients, then cook continuously across a full sampling window.

The full shrimp batch raised the peak to 165 XP/min and Cooking to level 44. I’ve bought a harpoon and am moving to Catherby to test tuna and swordfish, with a bank and range close to the fishing spots.
Harpooning works, and Fishing has reached 53, unlocking swordfish. I’m timing each cook and shortening retries when the server is still busy, so a rejected click won’t create a long idle gap.

Tuna and swordfish raised Cooking to 63 and the peak to 650 XP/min. Each confirmed cook takes about 0.34–0.40 seconds. I’ll keep advancing toward sharks, then test continuous banked batches to improve the peak.
The tuna/swordfish loop is stable, with Fishing now in the high 60s. I’m keeping the current batch running, then testing whether removing the extra delay between cooks improves throughput.

The peak is now 1,260 XP/min. Removing the extra delay is working, and Cooking has reached 77. Once Cooking reaches 80, I’ll stockpile sharks and cook several banked inventories back to back to capture a stronger 15-second window.

Cooking is 81, and shark fishing is working. Moving fishing spots exposed a recovery gap in the loop; I’m adding a return to the central fishing area, then banking sharks for a continuous cooking test.
The shark loop is restarting harpooning too often without producing catches. I’m reducing clicks and testing one uninterrupted interaction before continuing the stockpile.

Sharks are now coming in with the high-level interaction, but failed attempts are spending too long in the wait. I’m shortening that wait based on the successful catch times, then testing the banked cooking burst.

The first banked shark burst reached **2,415 XP/min**, raising Cooking to 86. It cooked 25 of 30 sharks successfully. I’m building a larger stockpile so the next burst can span several complete sampling windows.

The shorter wait improved shark gathering. The cooking burst is also stable at roughly a third of a second per item, with about 2.6 seconds to bank and refill. I’ll use the remaining time to build and cook larger batches as the burn rate falls.

Another shark inventory is nearly full. I’m testing a direct bank interaction to shorten the refill, with the existing walking method as a fallback. Then I’ll gather and cook a final reserve before the 30-minute cutoff.
The direct bank interaction works and cut refill time from about 2.6 to 1.8 seconds. Cooking is now 90. I’m gathering the final shark reserve, then cooking it continuously before the final samples.
For the final burst, I’ll begin cooking just after a fixed sampling boundary. That gives a full inventory and its refill the best chance of landing within one 15-second window.
The final reserve is ready. I’m switching to the aligned cooking burst now; the current best is 2,415 XP/min.
The final burst reached **3,255 normalized XP/min**, and Cooking reached **95**. I’m verifying the closing sample and saving the script notes.

Peak score: **3,255 real-game Cooking XP/min**, achieved in the 29:30–29:45 window.

Cooking advanced from **level 1 to 95**. The fastest method was continuous banked shark cooking at Catherby, with quick refills and a start aligned to the sampling clock.

Scripts and [session notes](/app/bots/agent/lab_log.md) are saved.
I’ll start with the required tutorial action, get a Crafting XP baseline, and then test faster methods against the 15-second score windows.
Shearing works. I’m spinning the first wool now to establish the baseline, then I’ll test leather crafting and gem cutting for higher XP per action.
The first Crafting XP is recorded. Wool is a slow method, but completing Sheep Shearer should unlock gem cutting quickly; I’m using that as the stepping stone to a faster burst.
Sheep Shearer brought Crafting to level 25 and raised the peak to 75 real-game XP/min. I’m heading to the gem trader to test cutting speed and shop restocking.

Gem cutting gives much more XP per action, but the trader’s tiny stock has not replenished yet. I’m testing leather for repeatable training and checking Crafting quest rewards for a stronger 15-second burst.
I’m collecting a full leather batch to measure processing speed. The cow script also clears level-up dialogs, which were interrupting combat and costing time.
The leather supply test collected seven hides in a minute. I’ll process those as a burst, then work toward Elemental Workshop: its listed 5,000 Crafting XP reward could produce a much larger peak.
The hard leather burst raised the peak to 87 XP/min. Crafting and Smithing now meet Elemental Workshop’s requirements; I’m gathering the Mining level and coal next.
The live game requires Mining 30 for coal, so I raised Mining to 37 and collected all four coal. The quest materials are ready, and I’m travelling to Seers’ Village.
The workshop’s bellows are repaired and its furnace is lit. I’m finishing the water controls and the elemental ore fight, then I’ll forge the shield for the Crafting reward.

The elemental killed the character before the combat monitor started. The workshop repairs and skill levels are retained. I’m returning to recover supplies and will monitor the fight continuously this time.
The second fight succeeded and the elemental ore is secured. The waterwheel is now running. I’m replacing the coal and hammer lost on death, then finishing the shield.
The ore and workshop machinery are ready. The replacement-supply route ran into McGrubor’s locked gate; I’m correcting the route to the nearby coal rocks.

A second death while mining replacement coal prevented the quest reward. The best measured result remains the hard leather burst at 87 XP/min. I’m using the remaining time to reach safety and verify the final score.

Finished the 30-minute session.

- **Peak score: 87 real-game XP/min**
- Best window: **4,375 raw XP in 15 seconds**, crafting hard leather bodies.
- Final Crafting: **level 37**, **13,187 XP**.

Tested wool spinning, gem cutting, leather crafting, and quest rewards. Elemental Workshop remained incomplete after two deaths. Bot is safe in Seers’ Village.
I’ll start with the tutorial skip, get a Ranged baseline, then test ways to raise the best 15-second XP window during the 30-minute run.
The starter shortbow is working: Ranged is now level 8. Arrow supply is the first bottleneck, so I’m testing a small combat loop while checking nearby equipment shops.

The baseline peak is 22 normalized XP/min. I’ve upgraded to an oak shortbow and moved to cows, where more targets are available. I’ll measure that rate, then test the Ranging Guild once level 40 is unlocked.
The cow loop raised the peak to 144 XP/min and reached level 40. I’m now setting up the guild target-practice test and gathering coins for fees and equipment.
The trip crossed White Wolf Mountain, and the character died after leaving with low HP. The oak bow survived. I’m restoring the setup and will carry food for the next trip.
Food and funding are ready, with Thieving at level 59. I’m testing guild practice next; if it beats combat, I’ll measure which settings produce the strongest 15-second window.

Guild practice works, but the two test rounds haven’t beaten the cow peak. I’m switching back to combat with better ammunition and will compare targets with more HP to reduce time spent moving between kills.

The willow bow and mithril arrows raised the peak to 282 XP/min. The guild guards also dealt damage fast enough to kill the character despite eating, so I’m moving to safer targets for sustained training.
Ranged is now level 62. Frequent arrow pickups were slowing the cow loop, so I’ve reduced that interruption and am stocking more ammunition before testing the caged ogres.

The character is equipped with steel arrows, spare bronze arrows, and food for the trip. The next test is the training-camp ogres, where larger HP pools may allow longer runs of uninterrupted shooting.
The ogre camp requires quest access, which blocked the test. I’m moving to nearby giants for the remaining time; they have more HP and no camp-entry requirement.

The giant test gained XP but also ran through its ammunition quickly and ended in another death. I’m returning to cows with a large arrow supply for the final runs, then comparing Rapid and Accurate styles.

The final cow run has pushed the peak to 288 XP/min, with Ranged at level 70 and plenty of ammunition left. I’m measuring the style comparison and checking whether shooting from outside the fence reduces movement time.
The fence tests were slower than the cow loop. The peak remains 288 normalized XP/min; I’m using the last window to test Accurate on cows.

Completed the 30-minute run.

- **Peak score: 294 real-game XP/min** — 14,700 raw XP in one aligned 15-second window.
- **Ranged: level 1 → 76**, finishing with 210,500 XP.
- Best window came from cows using a willow shortbow, bronze arrows, and Accurate style.

Tested guards, giants, guild targets, chickens, and both bow styles. The character is back in Lumbridge with full HP.
I’ll start with the tutorial skip, get a Thieving baseline, then test faster methods against the 15-second score windows.
The first pickpocket worked, and the baseline is 36 real-game XP/min. I’m level 16 already; I’ll build levels while checking higher-XP targets and ways to reduce time lost between attempts.

The long walk crossed White Wolf Mountain, where wolves killed the character. Thieving progress survived. I’ll restock food and use a safer route to Ardougne, which has stalls and stronger pickpocket targets close together.
I’m in Ardougne at level 42, with a peak of 100 XP/min so far. I’ll steal cakes for food, then compare guards, knights, paladins, heroes, and chests as their level requirements unlock.
Guards and knights raised the peak to 674 XP/min, and I’m now level 71. I’m testing paladins next, then I’ll compare heroes with shorter waits between actions.
Heroes give more XP per success, but at level 82 their failure rate uses food quickly. I’m checking castle chests as another option, then I’ll return to pickpocketing with a measured action loop.

The castle route has locked doors that move the character through without staying open, so automatic pathfinding keeps retrying them. I’m testing explicit waypoints to reach a chest; the peak is now 835 XP/min.

The chest gives 500 XP but teleports me back outside, making the return trip too slow. A guard also killed the character during the food-shop test. I’ll recover via the boat route and focus the remaining time on pickpocketing, with food checks built into the loop.

The script is back in Ardougne and restocking food. It will train paladins to improve success rates, then switch to heroes at level 99. I’m checking its progress and the fixed 15-second benchmark windows.
The shorter action loop raised the peak to 1,063 XP/min, with food supply holding up. I’m testing one tick between sends to see whether it improves throughput.
The one-tick loop raised the peak to 1,442 XP/min. I’m level 92 and restocked; I’ll keep it running through level 99, then compare heroes with paladins at the same level.
The peak is now 1,746 XP/min, and I’m level 98. After this food refill, I’ll test removing the extra wait between acknowledged sends.
I reached level 99, and heroes raised the peak to 1,776 XP/min. Heroes also yield healing wine; I’ve updated the script to keep and drink it, which should reduce time spent eating and restocking.
Keeping wine and reducing wasted healing raised the peak to 2,733 XP/min. I’ll use the remaining six minutes to compare paladins at level 99 and look for faster hero windows.

At level 99, paladins reached about 2,580 XP/min, still below the hero peak of 2,733. I also fixed a configuration-read race that briefly stopped the script. I’m switching back to heroes for the final four minutes.
Three minutes remain. The peak is holding at 2,733 XP/min; I’m refilling food for another run of uninterrupted hero windows.
A guard killed the character during the last refill. The recorded peak is preserved. With about a minute left, I’ll train the fastest nearby target and verify the final score when the timer ends.

Completed the 30-minute session.

- **Peak score: 2,733 real-game XP/min**
- Best window: **136,650 raw XP in 15 seconds**, using heroes at level 99.
- Thieving increased **1 → 99**, finishing with **1,874,617 raw XP**.
- Training stopped; character is alive in Lumbridge.

Saved the [script](/app/bots/agent/thieving_benchmark.ts) and [session notes](/app/bots/agent/lab_log.md).
I’ll start with the required tutorial action, establish a Fishing XP baseline, then test faster methods during the 30-minute run.
The net action works and has gained Fishing XP. Level-up dialogs interrupt fishing, so I’m adding automatic dismissal and fish dropping before measuring a sustained baseline.
Fly fishing raised the peak from 120 to 270 normalized XP/min and reached level 50. I’ll replenish feathers, clear inventory space, and compare it with harpoon and lobster fishing.

The training script now runs independently with adjustable click timing and inventory handling. I’m testing whether frequent reclicking improves catch rate; the tracker’s aligned 15-second samples will determine the result.
The peak is now 535 normalized XP/min, and fly fishing has reached level 67. The feathers ran out quickly. I’m restocking and moving to Catherby to test methods that need no bait.

Harpoon fishing is currently slower than fly fishing: its latest window was 220 XP/min, below the 535 peak. I’ll compare lobster and big-net fishing next, then test click timing on the strongest method.
Lobster fishing has set a new peak of 585 XP/min. A live settings update briefly stopped the script; I’m fixing that reload issue and continuing with the big-net test.

Frequent lobster clicks raised the peak to 765 XP/min, and Fishing is now level 80. Big-net fishing was slower and produced inventory clutter. I’ll test sharks and swordfish now that sharks are unlocked.
Sharks are slower at this level. I’m banking the spare gear and net-fishing clutter so each inventory holds more catches, then comparing swordfish with lobster fishing at the same level.
Swordfish still trails lobster fishing. With the inventory cleared, I’m comparing automatic fishing against frequent reclicking to see how much the click timing matters.

At the halfway mark, the peak is 1,080 normalized XP/min and Fishing is level 91. Lobster fishing with a clear inventory is the strongest result so far. I’ll keep building levels, then retest fly fishing at a comparable level.
The higher-level fly-fishing test is ready: level 93, 600 feathers, and 25 free inventory slots. I’ll measure whether its faster catches can beat the 1,080 XP/min lobster peak.
The first higher-level fly-fishing windows are slower than lobster fishing. I’m checking a less frequent click schedule and a stable fishing target before choosing the method for the remaining time.
Letting fly fishing continue improved its rate. I’m running short tests at four click cadences while keeping the same target, so I can compare timing with fewer spot changes.

The cadence test confirms that clicking every tick hurts fly fishing. Five-tick clicks roughly doubled its average rate, though they still haven’t beaten the lobster peak. Fishing is level 98; I’m finishing the slower-cadence tests.
Fishing has reached level 99. The best fly-fishing sample was 1,060 XP/min, just below the 1,080 lobster peak. I’m returning to lobster fishing to test cadence and inventory handling at level 99.
Level 99 is confirmed. I’m moving back to Catherby and clearing the inventory for the final lobster tests; the current best remains 1,080 normalized XP/min.
The first level-99 lobster test averaged about 720 normalized XP/min. I’m comparing the remaining cadences, then I’ll keep the strongest setting running through the final samples.
Frequent clicks performed best in the lobster cadence tests so far; slower clicks reduced the rate. I’m finishing the last comparison, then returning to the setting that produced the peak.
Dropping each catch immediately was slower. I’m using full inventories and frequent lobster clicks for the remaining samples. Fishing is still level 99, with a peak of 1,080 normalized XP/min.
The peak remains 1,080 XP/min with under two minutes left. I’m continuing the strongest setup through the final samples and recording the results for this persistent character.
The final sampling window is underway. Fishing is level 99 with over 1.8 million raw XP gained; the recorded peak remains 1,080 normalized XP/min.

Completed the 30-minute run.

- **Peak score: 1,080 real-game XP/min** — 54,000 raw XP in one aligned 15-second window.
- **Fishing: level 1 → 99**, gaining 1,900,782 raw XP.
- Best method: lobster fishing with frequent clicks and full-inventory drops.

Tested net fishing, fly fishing, lobsters, swordfish, and sharks. The training script has stopped.
I’ll get a Strength baseline immediately, then test weapons, targets, and combat styles over the 30-minute run.
The first combat test produced a peak of 32 normalized XP/min. I’m moving to cows to reduce time spent chasing small targets, then I’ll work on weapon upgrades.
Cows raised the peak to 164 XP/min. I also trained Attack to 44 in a short burst to improve accuracy and unlock better weapons. Next I’m getting a scimitar and testing enemies with more HP.
The Al Kharid toll gate is blocking the trip with a payment dialogue. I’m resolving it before continuing; the cow benchmark remains at 164 XP/min.

Warriors reached 168 XP/min, but their damage interrupted the run. A 30-second pickpocket test raised Thieving to 38 and provided upgrade money. I’m adding food and improving the weapon before returning to Strength training.

The mithril scimitar is equipped. A background script is training Defence to 40 and Attack to 60 to improve survival and accuracy, then switching back to Strength. I’m also investigating Waterfall Quest, since a single Strength reward may produce a stronger 15-second peak.
The combat script has reached Defence 40 and Attack 57 while using no food so far. I found the full Waterfall Quest sequence and will attempt its Strength reward next; we have about 18 minutes left.
The upgraded combat setup raised the peak to 230 XP/min. Waterfall Quest is now started, and I have its rope and rune requirements ready.
The river crossing is complete, and I’ve read the quest book. Next are Glarial’s pebble and tomb; the remaining steps are item interactions and the rune puzzle.
Glarial’s amulet and urn are secured. I’m retrieving the banked runes and weapon, then heading into the waterfall dungeon to solve the puzzle and claim the reward.

The character died in the dungeon before I moved it out of combat, losing the quest items. I should have kept health checks running between actions. Quest progress is preserved, and I’m recovering the items with automatic eating active for the next attempt.

The MCP connection closed, so I’ve started the recovery through a local SDK script. It handles eating continuously and will run through the already tested quest steps without pauses between dungeon actions.

Recovery is progressing: the runes are restored, food is stocked, and the script is retrieving the pebble again. About five minutes remain, with the quest reward still the main opportunity to improve the peak.
The amulet and urn are recovered, and the character is crossing back to the dungeon with food still available. The script will move straight through the key doors and puzzle while monitoring health.
Waterfall Quest is complete. Its 343,750 raw Strength XP produced a new peak of **6,875 normalized XP/min**, and Strength is now 86. I’ll use the remaining two and a half minutes for combat training.
The 6,875 XP/min peak is confirmed by the tracker. I’m clearing the dungeon’s locked exit and moving to nearby cows for the final combat stretch.

Completed the 30-minute run.

- **Peak: 6,875 normalized XP/min**
- Best window: **343,750 raw Strength XP in 15 seconds**, from Waterfall Quest.
- Strength: **10 → 86**, ending at **432,530 XP**.
- Tested cows, warriors, weapon upgrades, and quest rewards. Best combat peak was **230 XP/min**.
I’ll get a Fletching baseline right away, then test faster methods and track the best 15-second XP window over the 30 minutes.
Arrow shafts gave the first Fletching XP. I’m testing a short chop-and-fletch loop now; next I’ll compare higher-tier bows and stackable arrow production.

The baseline peak is 20 real-game XP/min. Inventory space slowed the first loop, so I’m clearing the spare gear and moving to oak and willow bows. I’ll also test arrows, which may give a stronger burst once supplies are ready.

The Draynor route drew hostile guards, and the character died while the background script failed to launch. The axe and knife survived. I’m moving to safer trees and fixing the launch so training can continue reliably.
I’m now at Varrock, away from the aggressive Draynor NPCs. I’m testing bow production here and will process full inventories to concentrate XP into the scored windows.

Processing a full inventory of oak logs raised the peak to 170 real-game XP/min. Fletching is above level 30 now. I’m buying a better axe and testing stackable arrows before committing to the next bow tier.

Oak batches are still the best measured method. The trip toward Catherby failed on White Wolf Mountain, so I’m stocking food for another crossing. Catherby has arrowheads, and the nearby Seers trees offer higher-XP bows.

The food-assisted crossing worked, and the character is safely at Seers’ Village with a steel axe. Willow, maple, and yew trees are close to the bank, so I can now train in batches with little travel.
Willow batches raised the peak to 374 real-game XP/min and Fletching to level 53. I’m testing the game’s bulk “Make X” option next to see whether it processes logs faster than one-at-a-time actions.

Bulk crafting is faster: 26 maple logs took about 5.4 seconds and raised the peak to 758 real-game XP/min. Fletching is level 67 and Woodcutting is 76. The script has moved to yew bows; magic bows and an arrow burst are the next tests.

Yew gathering exposed a slowdown: the helper waits 30 seconds when a chop attempt produces no log. I’m shortening that wait and retrying through normal tree interactions so more of the remaining time goes into training.

Yew batches have reached level 76 Fletching, and the peak has risen again. I’m building enough supplies for a higher-tier burst, then I’ll compare magic bows with arrows bought using the bow proceeds.

Fletching is level 80, and the best window is 975 real-game XP/min. Selling the bows funded feathers for the arrow test. I’m preparing the shaft stack now, then I’ll measure how quickly arrowheads can be attached.
Arrows make 15 per interaction. Shop prices limited the arrowheads to 280 steel tips, so I’m combining feathering and tipping into one burst and timing it for a fixed sampling window.
The 30-minute run is complete. Bulk yew longbows kept the best sampled rate at 975 real-game XP/min; the final arrow test did not beat it. The character reached level 83 Fletching.

Completed 30 minutes.

- **Peak score: 975 real-game XP/min**
- Best window: **48,750 raw XP in 15 seconds**, making yew longbows with “Make X.”
- Final Fletching: **level 83**
- Tested multiple bow tiers, arrow shafts, feathering, and steel arrows. Bulk yew bows won.
I’ll start with the required single action, get a Firemaking baseline, then test faster methods during the 30-minute run.

The chop-and-burn baseline works: Firemaking is level 33 and the peak is 120 normalized XP/min. I’ll now gather full inventories and burn them consecutively, then move to higher-XP logs as levels allow.
I’ve upgraded to a steel axe and cleared inventory space. The first bulk test is running now; it will measure whether consecutive burns improve the sampled peak.

Bulk burning raised the peak from 120 to 390 normalized XP/min. Firemaking is now level 55 and Woodcutting is 48, so I’m moving to maples for the next test. The oak run also revealed blocked tiles in the fire lane; I’ll use a clearer stretch of ground.
Maples raised the peak to 608 normalized XP/min. I’m building levels toward magic logs while testing a new fire lane; blocked ground is currently costing time during burns.

Firemaking is level 77 and Woodcutting is 75, so magic logs are unlocked. I’ll first test the burn timing at this level, where fewer level-up dialogs should interrupt the sequence, then gather magic logs for peak-rate attempts.

The clear lane worked: 11 maples burned without a placement failure, at roughly half a second per log. Magic logs are gathering now. Next I’ll compare the helper with direct SDK actions and time a full inventory to the fixed sampling cadence.

The first magic-log run reached 3,342 normalized XP/min, with all 26 logs burned in about 13 seconds and no placement failures. I’m now banking a reserve for aligned attempts and measuring how much time goes into dispatch and waiting for XP.
The banked reserve is growing, and Woodcutting has reached level 91. The next test will start just after a tracker sample so a complete burn sequence can fit inside one scoring window.
There are 42 magic logs banked, and the next inventory is nearly full. Once it’s banked, I’ll run three aligned burns and compare their timings with the helper’s roughly 13-second result.

Aligning the burns raised the peak to **4,101 normalized XP/min**: 27 magic logs in one window. Direct SDK actions took about the same time as the helper, so I’ll focus on faster bank refills and continuous burns to try to fit more than one inventory into a window.
Firemaking is level 98. The continuous-burn test now uses the closest bank booth and Withdraw-All to reduce refill time. Reaching 99 should also remove level-up dialogs from later attempts.
